Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function
Derivatives: derivative of a function, derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions by definition (simple forms)
Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives
Geometric interpretation of derivative; monotonicity of a function, interval of monotonicity, extreme values of a function, concavity, points of inflection

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The derivative's geometric meaning is dynamic: the tangent is the limiting secant, its slope f′(a), the normal its perpendicular partner, and a vertical tangent is the derivative's finite failure. The sign of f′ is a local fact that the Mean Value Theorem promotes to global monotonicity, and the same number reads as a physical rate with units.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Tangent: y − f(a) = f′(a)(x − a); Normal: y − f(a) = −(1/f′(a))(x − a) - f′ > 0 on (a, b) ⟹ f strictly increasing on (a, b)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Computing $f'(a)$ and reporting it as the angle of inclination, forgetting to apply $\theta=\tan^{-1}(f'(a))$.  ·  Saying a horizontal tangent guarantees a maximum; it marks a candidate only.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Computing $f'(a)$ and reporting it as the angle of inclination, forgetting to apply $\theta=\tan^{-1}(f'(a))$.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The touching test fails*** - y = x^3 at 0 touches the x-axis and crosses it; the limit-of-secants definition survives where the folk definition dies.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Computing the normal's slope as $-\frac1{f'(a)}$ when $f'(a)=0$, which is division by zero — the normal is vertical instead.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Work through the authored practice problems and re-derive each key formula from the definition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Tangent and normal in one breath: slope m, then -1/m, both through the same point.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Find the tangent line to y = x² at (2, 4) and the normal line there.** — **Slope:** y′ = 2x ⟹ at x = 2: m = **4**. **Tangent:** y − 4 = 4(x − 2) ⟹ **y = 4x − 4**. **Normal:** slope −1/4 ⟹ y − 4 = −(1/4)(x − 2) ⟹ **x + 4y = 18**.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Find the tangent and normal to y = x³ − 2x at x = 1, and determine where the tangent crosses the x-axis.** — **Point:** f(1) = 1 − 2 = −1 ⟹ (1, −1). **Slope:** f′ = 3x² − 2 ⟹ f′(1) = **1**. **Tangent:** y + 1 = 1(x − 1) ⟹ **y = x − 2**; it crosses the x-axis at x = 2.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Quote the units when interpreting a derivative as a rate - the mark is for the reading, not the number.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The tangent is defined dynamically - the limiting secant - not by a touching count.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Tangent slope = f'(a) = limit of secant slopes; tangent line y - f(a) = f'(a)(x - a); normal slope -1/f'(a); vertical tangent when f' -> +-inf. Corners have two half-tangents. f' > 0 on an interval implies increasing (MVT converts local signs to global monotonicity). f' = 0 means stationary, not necessarily extreme.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The MVT is the bridge from local derivative signs to global monotonicity.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): For f(x) = |x|, describe the tangent geometry at x = 0 and connect it to the derivative's failure.** — **Right side:** slope +1 ⟹ half-tangent y = x for x ≥ 0. **Left side:** slope −1 ⟹ half-tangent y = −x for x ≤ 0.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): A body's position is s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t (metres, seconds). Find the velocity at t = 2 and interpret its sign; find when the body momentarily stops.** — **Velocity:** v(t) = s′(t) = 3t² − 12t + 9 = 3(t − 1)(t − 3).…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to the Derivative's Geometric Meaning This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to the derivative's geometric interpretation: tangent slope, increasing/decreasing, and the rate reading in one page.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Tangent slope:** f′(a) = slope of the tangent at (a, f(a)) — the limiting position of secants through (a, f(a)) and (a+h, f(a+h)). - **Tangent line:** y − f(a) = f′(a)(x − a); **normal line:** slope −1/f′(a) (f′(a) ≠ 0); vertical tangent when f′ → ±∞.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Slope as the Limit of Secants - The tangent is **not** "the line touching at one point" — circles aside, that folk definition fails (cubics touch and cross). The precise definition is dynamic: the secant through two nearby points, with the second point sliding in. The limit of chords is the tangent; the limit of their slopes is f′(a).…

rows.text: NEB-style practice beyond the verified PYQs recorded on the parent canonical.  ·  A vertical tangent is the derivative's failure to be finite - and that failure is information.  ·  Find the tangent to y = x² at (2, 4).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Find the tangent and normal to y = x³ − 2x at x = 1.  ·  Interpret f′(3) = −5 for f(t) measuring temperature in °C at time t in minutes.  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — The Sign of f′ Is a Global Statement - **Local sign, global consequence:** if f′ > 0 at *every* point of an interval, the function is strictly increasing on the whole interval — the Mean Value Theorem converts the local derivative data into a global monotonicity statement.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — tangent/normal at a point:** evaluate f and f′, write both lines. - **Type B — corner geometry:** one-sided slopes, two half-tangents, no tangent. - **Type C — sign table sketching:** f′ signs ⟹ increasing/decreasing intervals.…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"Tangent touches at exactly one point":** the folk definition — the limit-of-secants definition is the real one. **"f′ = 0 means a max or min":** it means stationary; classification needs the second derivative or a sign study.  ·  **f'(x) as geometry — the classified readings** | Sign/size of f' | Curve behaviour | Consequence | |---|---|---| | f' > 0 | Rising as x increases | Increasing function on that interval | | f' < 0 | Falling | Decreasing interval | | f' = 0 | Horizontal tangent | Stationary point: max, min or terrace | | |f'| large |…
